newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline up, traded at $28.75.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline up, traded at $28.75.

text.p: Gasoline prices edged up on the back of crude and firm sentiment amid aggressive buying, traders said on Friday.
Gasoline firmed with a Japanese trader buying 100,000 92-octane unleaded barrels at $28.75 per barrel fob Singapore lifting March 22-26 from a Swiss trader.
The last deal on the grade, on Monday, was at $28.20 for 80,000-barrels lifting March 19-23.

Offers into Saudi Aramco's import tender to buy up to 1.5 million barrels of 95-octane leaded gasoline in April were heard at $7.00-$8.00 per barrel c-and-f Ras Tanura over Singapore naphtha fob quotes, traders said. The tender closed March 4 and validity is until March 12.

Traders said the Singapore market was unable to supply the tender requirements, and cargoes would have to come from Europe as the Mediterranean is tight with nearly 100,000 tonnes already going into India in March.

A major's Yanbu cargo lifting in March was partially destined for Singapore, possibly to cover turnaround shortfalls. Sellers - a Swiss trader, a Dutch trader, a European major and a South Korean refiner - rumoured to have the best offers into Taiwan's reformate buy tender which was awarded Thursday at close to $29.00 per barrel c-and-f Taiwan, all denied having won.
But traders said Taiwan's purchase of 500,000 barrels should keep the market tight in first half April.
Naphtha swaps in April rose to $22.60/$22.80 per barrel from $22.50/$22.75 on Thursday, basically with crude, traders said.
"Naphtha prices are holding... the excitement of the arb cargoes is over," said one trader on reports last week of up to 200,000 tonnes arriving from the West in April.
Another trader however said arbitrage cargoes were being offered in the market, but no sellers were able to confirm.
